original_card.question: Does one changed supplier or assembly claim lack a source-bound independent check of a specific new implication?
methods: Reconstruct the rank ledger from original operations rather than trusting its aggregate.
Implement certified moment inequalities through a different exact enclosure method.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Demonstrate independence, source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls. Name the existing checks and the missing coverage. More digits or another equivalent evaluation of an unchanged root is not by itself new verification coverage.

first_step.inspect: Record the selected certificate and complex_profile rather than taking a PR headline as input.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: List the existing independent checks for the exact selected or candidate sources. Pick a new changed input, missing binding or distinct failure mode; stop with a handoff if the proposed arithmetic check is already covered.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Independent pricing prevents unsupported frontier claims and can reveal genuine accounting slack.
allowed_variations: Reconstruct either a source ledger or a numeric enclosure with a different method.
scope_change_triggers: Importing the primary function and calling its output independent verification.

actual_scope: Independent, source-bound check of a new finite implication on the joint-query-controller line: PR2389's classification of optimal 66-port terminal read sets for the QQ16 common-first-axis hidden-input family (threshold 66, exactly 45 sets, 22 mandatory ports, 29 nuisance coordinates, port 77 swaps for 44 ports) and the rank(H|V)=66 premise of PR2354/PR2389, rebuilt from main's sources with different methods (complement/column-matroid classification; owner bit-function independence certificate), plus a written audit of PR2389's adaptive argument.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for an independent check of a changed supplier/assembly claim's moment or rank ledger. Priority revision 4 asks verification to target an unproved or unreviewed new implication; PR2389 (opened 2026-10-15) makes new finite claims with only an author-run verifier, so this package checks those claims instead of a supplier moment. It is an independent re-derivation by a different route, not a new construction or kappa.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the joint-query-controller card: the QQ16 hidden-input family is a current obstruction to cheaper restored controllers. An independently checked 66-port threshold and 45-set classification fixes which read sets any favorable native access bill must use (PR2389 open question 1) before anyone prices them.
stop_rule: Stop at 09:14Z experiment deadline; if G/f_b could not be rebuilt from main sources by 08:55Z, inherit rank 66 (labelled); any mismatch reported as a concrete discrepancy only. Both were rebuilt in time; no pivot used.
evidence: verify.py (stdlib, exact) reproduces every compared PR2389/PR2354 finite claim from main's pinned sources: 47 first-axis groups, axis-2 group of 30 ports with rank 8, group rank sum 74, dim V 88, ker(H|V)=ker R_C of dimension 22, rank(H|V)=66 via a 47x47 0/1 owner minor of determinant 2^62 on identity + 46 registered owners, exactly 45 optimal sets, 22 mandatory ports, 29 nuisance coordinates, coloop 77, 44 port-77 swaps, dual vector (-1,0,1,0,1,0,1,0) with w r_77=-4. 10 negative controls are rejected. No discrepancy found. The written audit of the adaptive argument is in README.md.
author: thakrarsagar
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic, model Claude Opus 5.5): derivation, implementation, checking and writing. No code from PR2354 or PR2389 was imported or copied; their READMEs/RESULTs were read to state the audited claims and to locate the source members. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Is the 45-set classification stable under the full ordered QQ16 observation contract, i.e. do any of the 29 nuisance coordinates C-{77} carry a second hidden-input family that defeats all 45 sets at once?
open_questions.why_it_matters: All 45 optimal sets omit exactly the same 29 ports; one witness supported there would make every family-optimal set insufficient for arbitrary QQ16 inputs.
open_questions.first_step: Search ker R_U vectors supported on C-{77} union a second axis group for a target that is nonzero after the ordered F0/B1 maps (PR2384's second-axis witness is the nearest template).
open_questions.blocked_by: Requires the native ordered maps beyond the first-axis family; this package does not replay them.

open_questions.question: Which structured owner class certifies independence of the 47 first-axis bit functions? On the 768 registered route owners alone the rank is 44 (45 with the identity); the certificate needs 29 non-route registered owners.
open_questions.why_it_matters: A structured certificate would explain the power-of-two determinant 2^62 and show which cover translations carry the 3 missing directions, which matters for any owner-restricted reader model.
open_questions.first_step: Classify the registered non-route maps by their action on the 47 axes and find a minimal set that adds the 3 missing directions to the route-owner span.

open_questions.question: What lower bound holds for bounded-error or finite-promise readers on this family?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The transcript-fiber argument needs exactness on all of V over Q; physical inputs are bounded integers, where the fiber c+K_S can leave the promise set.
open_questions.first_step: Fix a finite coefficient box and an input distribution and compute the distributional decision-tree bound for a reduced instance.
open_questions.blocked_by: No agreed input distribution or promise set for QQ16 inputs.
